forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Non-treasury investment income increasingly dependent on usable reserves, rising from 63% to 78%.
news_drafts.lead: The proportion of usable reserves required to support non-treasury investment income rises from 63% in 2025/26 to 78% in 2026/27. The indicator monitors the availability of reserves to cover income from commercial property, and is not measured in later years.

news_drafts.headline: Commercial property investment reserve depleted from £3.2m to zero within three years.
news_drafts.lead: The reserve designated to cover voids and maintenance works on commercial properties falls from £3,162k in 2025/26 to £452k in 2026/27 and zero from 2027/28 onwards. The depletion is rapid and material.

news_drafts.headline: Commercial and housing investments showing £27m negative equity in 2025/26.
news_drafts.lead: The security of the council's commercial and housing investments shows a deficit of £27,027k in 2025/26, with assets worth less than the debt outstanding against them. This indicator is not reported for subsequent years.

findings.headline: Non-treasury investment income increasingly dependent on usable reserves, rising from 63% to 78%.
findings.detail: The proportion of usable reserves required to support non-treasury investment income rises from 63% in 2025/26 to 78% in 2026/27. The indicator monitors the availability of reserves to cover income from commercial property, and is not measured in later years.
findings.matters: Rising reliance on reserves to underpin investment income, particularly as the commercial property reserve above is simultaneously depleted to zero, shows deteriorating financial flexibility. Lenders assess reserve adequacy; finance directors watch similar pressures across similar investments.
findings.quote: Non Treasury investment income as a proportion of Usable Reserves Investment Strategy 63% 78% n/a n/a

findings.headline: Commercial property investment reserve depleted from £3.2m to zero within three years.
findings.detail: The reserve designated to cover voids and maintenance works on commercial properties falls from £3,162k in 2025/26 to £452k in 2026/27 and zero from 2027/28 onwards. The depletion is rapid and material.
findings.matters: Rapid depletion of a protective reserve is material, especially given the negative equity in the same portfolio shown above. Lenders question whether this reflects planned consumption or unexpected performance affecting the investment base.
findings.quote: Commercial Property Investments Reserve Levels Investment Strategy 3,162 452 0 0

findings.headline: Commercial and housing investments showing £27m negative equity in 2025/26.
findings.detail: The security of the council's commercial and housing investments shows a deficit of £27,027k in 2025/26, with assets worth less than the debt outstanding against them. This indicator is not reported for subsequent years.
findings.matters: Negative equity in major investment holdings signals asset quality concerns. Lenders are concerned about the council's exposure. Finance directors at other councils would want to know if this reflects broader commercial property market stress or portfolio-specific issues.
findings.quote: Security of Commercial and Housing Investments Investment Strategy (27,027) n/a n/a n/a

findings.headline: Proportion of financing costs to net revenue stream rising from 123% to 140% over four years.
findings.detail: Interest and MRP costs as a percentage of net revenue budget start at 123% in 2025/26, decline to 120% in 2026/27, then rise steeply to 135% in 2027/28 and 140% in 2028/29. This upward trajectory in debt service costs relative to revenue is material.
findings.matters: Escalating financing costs relative to revenue budget is a critical sustainability indicator for lenders assessing affordability. The trajectory suggests growing pressure on council finances as borrowing increases combine with rising debt service obligations.
findings.quote: Proportion of financing costs to net revenue stream Capital Strategy 123% 120% 135% 140%

findings.headline: Gross borrowing rising from £620m to £813m, an increase of £193m over four years.
findings.detail: Capital financing requirement and gross borrowing both showing sustained growth, with in-year borrowing requirement jumping from £34,775k in 2025/26 to £63,609k in 2026/27 and remaining elevated at £62,956k-£66,680k for subsequent years. This represents a 31% increase in total borrowing over the period.
findings.matters: Lenders assess total debt burden and trajectories when monitoring credit risk. Finance directors at other councils need visibility of how peers are managing significant borrowing increases alongside major capital programmes.
